subject: Culture
title: Diwali and Prosperity Gifts
description: A 60-second lesson on Diwali and Prosperity Gifts.

hook.text: During Diwali, Indian families exchange boxes of sweets so elaborate they rival wedding cakes.

buildup.text: Diwali celebrates the victory of light over darkness. Gifts invoke Lakshmi, goddess of wealth and fortune.

discovery.text: Corporate Diwali gifting is a billion-dollar industry. Companies send hampers to clients encoded with loyalty signals.

twist.text: Gold purchases spike during Diwali. Buying gold on this day is considered so auspicious that jewelers extend hours.

climax.text: Diwali gifting obligations can strain middle-class budgets. Social pressure turns celebration into financial stress.

punchline.text: Festival generosity has a price tag attached.

quiz.question: Which goddess is associated with Diwali prosperity gifts?

details.summary: Diwali gift-giving centers on prosperity symbols — sweets, dry fruits, gold, and new clothes signal abundance and good fortune. Corporate Diwali gifting in India has become a multi-billion dollar industry.
details.whyItMatters: Diwali gifting reveals how South Asian culture intertwines spirituality with prosperity. The festival's commercial scale makes it one of the world's most significant gift-giving events.
takeaways: Diwali is India's largest gift-giving occasion, surpassing all others
Corporate Diwali gifting is a multi-billion dollar industry
Gold purchases during Diwali are considered especially auspicious

faq.question: What are traditional Diwali gifts?
faq.answer: Traditional gifts include boxes of Indian sweets (mithai), dry fruits, new clothes, gold jewelry or coins, silver items, and decorative items for the home. Lakshmi (goddess of wealth) is worshipped during Diwali, so gifts related to prosperity are especially appropriate.

faq.question: How has Diwali gifting become commercialized?
faq.answer: Corporate Diwali gifting has exploded into a multi-billion dollar industry. Companies give employees and partners elaborate gift hampers, branded merchandise, and cash bonuses. E-commerce platforms run massive Diwali sales rivaling Black Friday.
